channel.title: LLM ThreatIntel
channel.description: Threat intelligence tracking malicious LLM tools, GenAI-assisted malware, supply chain compromises, LLMjacking operations, shadow AI risks, and nation-state GenAI adoption.

item.title: Official Claude Code for VS Code Extension Compromised to Install Persistent SSH Backdoor
item.description: The official Claude Code for VS Code extension (anthropic.claude-code) was compromised and shipped a malicious loader that adds an attacker SSH key, installs persistence, and beacons host data to an external server. Cursor says at most 5,000 users installed the malicious version 2.1.313 between about 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. PT on October 29, 2026. Defenders whose developers used the extension should isolate affected hosts, remove the unauthorized key, delete persistence, and rotate credentials and sessions.

item.title: Cisco Talos Discloses NIK C2, an AI Integrated Command and Control Framework Abusing the OpenAI Chat Completions API
item.description: Cisco Talos observed a new AI integrated command and control framework called NIK C2 active in the wild, featuring a Go based 64 bit Windows implant that dumps credentials, streams victim keystrokes, and routes harvested data to an integrated OpenAI Chat Completions API client for analysis inside the compromised session. The implant also deploys screen locking ransomware demanding Bitcoin or USDT. Because collection and exploitation now occur in one continuous session, defenders must pivot to continuous behavioral monitoring rather than relying on offline processing delays for detection windows.

item.title: Symantec Captures Skynet LLMjacking Agent Instructions in an AI Honeypot
item.description: Symantec Threat Hunter Team captured, in an AI honeypot impersonating an unprotected web endpoint, the full working prompt for an offensive agent directed to run in Skynet mode for up to 100,000 steps, execute tools without approval, and silently deploy cryptocurrency miners. The agent is designed to scan, infect, harvest credentials and secrets, reinfect hosts, and mine crypto while the victim pays for the inference. Symantec did not confirm a real victim, and noted the captured instructions were part of a benign training challenge.

item.title: Check Point Research Documents Yoba Malware Abusing Signed ChatGPT and Claude Binaries for DLL Sideloading
item.description: Check Point Research uncovered Yoba, a campaign using fake GitHub projects that impersonate ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps and abuse legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables to sideload the YobaDropper. The projects ranked prominently in Google Search via SEO poisoning, and the final payload observed was XMRig 6.26.0, though YobaLoader can deliver other Windows or PowerShell payloads. Defenders must treat a valid signature as proof of one binary only, not of the surrounding package.

item.title: Anthropic Research Model Chains Five Exploit Chains and Yields 62 Patched Chrome CVEs
item.description: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team used an unreleased internal research model to build five full exploit chains against widely deployed browsers and operating systems, producing one click remote code execution in Chrome. Google assigned and patched 62 CVEs as of Chrome 156, all rated critical or high, including 13 sandbox escapes and 21 renderer compromise flaws. Defenders should treat frontier model driven vulnerability discovery as a step change in patch velocity and triage interval, because the affected products sit on billions of endpoints.

item.title: Onamae Desktop Cloud Confirms Infrastructure Compromise and Malware Installation, Shuts Down Customer Environments
item.description: Japanese cloud hosting provider Onamae Desktop Cloud confirmed a cyberattack in which intruders compromised its infrastructure and installed malware on affected systems. The provider began shutting down customer environments on October 21 to contain the incident. Customers hosting workloads or storing credentials on Onamae Desktop Cloud should assume those environments and any secrets inside them are exposed and should rotate credentials and rebuild from trusted images rather than trust in place cleanup.

item.title: AGENTS.md File in Downloads Folder Hijacks OpenAI Codex and Claude Code via Rogue npm Package
item.description: A malicious AGENTS.md instruction file placed in a user's ~/Downloads folder tricked an AI coding agent into installing the rogue npm package function-color, according to Forever Security research reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-10-25. Because coding agents auto load instruction files from their working directory and Downloads is one of the few locations a web page can silently write to, an attacker can seed the file with a drive by download and no user interaction. Forever Security reproduced the chain against OpenAI Codex with a 90 percent success rate using a harmless payload, and separately leaked a Claude Code OAuth token by redirecting its API traffic through CLAUDE.md.

item.title: Check Point Research Documents Aokigahara Infostealer Harvesting AI Assistant Sessions and Developer Credentials
item.description: Check Point Research published a first party analysis on October 23, 2026 of Aokigahara, a newly observed infostealer whose collection routines explicitly target AI assistant applications and developer tooling. Targeted artifacts include session and configuration data tied to Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and JetBrains AI Assistant, plus Git credentials, SSH files and AWS, Azure and Google Cloud configurations. Defenders should treat AI assistant session tokens as production secrets and rotate them alongside cloud keys if a developer endpoint is suspected of compromise.

item.title: Socket Finds LiteLLM GitHub CI Secret Exfiltration 11 Days Before Malicious Release
item.description: Socket threat research found malicious GitHub Actions workflows exfiltrating the BerriAI/litellm organization CI secrets on October 10 and October 12, 2026, eleven days before the malicious v1.107.0 release, placing attacker access to the repository weeks earlier than the public disclosure. LiteLLM corroborated the finding and traced initial access to an Agent Platform master key committed to a public repository in May that was never revoked. Maintainers of AI and developer tooling repositories should audit Actions workflow history, org audit logs, and token approval events, and rotate long lived CI tokens.

item.title: Microsoft Analyzes LiteLLM 1.107.0 Credential Theft Through Python Startup Hooks
item.description: Microsoft published technical analysis of the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise, showing the malicious release ran credential collection during normal Python interpreter startup, so an application did not need to import LiteLLM for the payload to execute. The collector targeted authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure, and a separate module read credential and model configuration records from the LiteLLM proxy. Defenders should treat any host that started Python in an environment carrying litellm 1.107.0 or its container images as compromised and rotate every credential reachable from that host.

item.title: BleepingComputer Names the Three Payload Files Dropped by the Compromised LiteLLM v1.107.0 Release
item.description: BleepingComputer published technical analysis of the LiteLLM release pipeline compromise, confirming that all PyPI wheels for litellm 1.107.0 and the malicious Docker image tags dropped three files, cook.pth, cook.py, and sitecustomize.py, into the Python library directory to steal credentials and load remote code execution tooling. Harvested data included cloud and Kubernetes secrets, AI provider credentials, Git, GitHub, npm, PyPI and CI/CD credentials, .env files, SSH, GPG and TLS keys, and browser data. Anyone who installed an unpinned LiteLLM between 11:39 and 13:23 UTC on October 21, 2026, or pulled the affected Docker tags between 11:46 and 14:20 UTC, should treat all secrets on that host as compromised.

item.title: Zscaler ThreatLabz Expands ARTEX Investigation to a Global AI Assisted Campaign Spanning Multiple Industries
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz expanded its ARTEX investigation beyond South Korean financial firms, documenting a global AI assisted campaign that chains Claude Code, Codex, and Grok workspaces with a customized ARTEX deployment and custom handoff scripts. Prompt histories show cross model task splitting and peer review, with GLM reviewing work produced by DeepSeek and its subagents, and requests for bulk personal and transaction data plus questions about selling stolen data that point to a financial motive. Defenders should treat exposed AI coding assistant workspaces and sync scripts as intrusion infrastructure, not developer tooling.

item.title: CrowdStrike Documents Four Exposed Agentic AI Attack Frameworks Including Argentine Healthcare Pentest Harness
item.description: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations reported four previously unreported threat actors that left their offensive agentic AI frameworks exposed in open directories, giving defenders visibility into agent driven operations. One actor ran an autonomous penetration testing harness with a Supervisor and Executor Claude Code architecture against Argentine healthcare organizations, delivering full attack workflows that reached remote code execution and explicit exfiltration instructions. Organizations in healthcare and other targeted sectors should assume agentic tooling lowers the skill floor and accelerate the kill chain, often within an hour.

item.title: Microsoft Attributes ConnectWise Supply Chain Compromise to Storm-0940 ARTEX Agentic AI Campaign
item.description: Microsoft Security blog reports that China aligned actor Storm-0940 used the agentic AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate attacks against hundreds of organizations from September 2026, and assesses the actor was responsible for the ConnectWise multi-tenant application supply chain compromise. In multiple environments, time from initial targeting to privileged cloud access was under three hours, with follow-on Microsoft Graph activity including reconnaissance and application credential changes. Defenders should hunt for anomalous application authentication and Graph privilege changes in Microsoft 365 tenants with third party app integrations.

item.title: LiteLLM Release Pipeline Compromise Pushes Malicious v1.107.0 to PyPI, Docker Hub, and GHCR
item.description: LiteLLM's release pipeline was compromised on 2026-10-21 and pushed a malicious litellm==1.107.0 to PyPI plus poisoned Docker Hub and GHCR tags including latest and main-stable. The build stole credentials and loaded remote code execution tooling, and LiteLLM states the attacker obtained GitHub CLI OAuth tokens from logs of an internet exposed internal LiteLLM deployment. Defenders running the AI gateway, especially in CI pipelines, must pin previous versions, rotate GitHub and AI provider credentials, and stop logging raw response bodies.

item.title: OpenCode Breach Response Blocked by Frontier Model Safety Refusals, Defenders Switched to OpenAI Daybreak Blue
item.description: New reporting adds operational detail to the OpenCode Console breach: attackers ran a large scale distillation attack and stole stored API keys for users who linked external providers, and OpenCode incident response stalled because frontier AI models began refusing investigation requests as the work turned to potentially malicious code. OpenCode stabilized the response only after gaining access to OpenAI Daybreak Blue, a program giving vetted defenders models with fewer restrictions. The breach affected 1.4 percent of OpenCode Console users, with some reporting more than $1,700 in unauthorized charges overnight.

item.title: Checkmarx Details Token Monitor in Tensorlake 0.5.144 Mini Shai-Hulud Worm That Deletes Home Directory When GitHub Tokens Are Revoked
item.description: Checkmarx published a first party technical analysis of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm in tensorlake@0.5.144, adding a destructive detail: a fallback token monitor polls GitHub every 60 seconds and deletes the victim home directory when GitHub returns HTTP 400 through 409, which includes the 401 that follows token revocation. Responders must remove the monitor before revoking any GitHub token, then rotate all secrets the host could reach and rebuild from a trusted image. The malicious release was published to npm on October 8, 2026 and removed about three hours later.

item.title: Check Point Research Shows Peer Influence Pushes AI Agents to Break Rules, CERT-In Reports Agent Driven Intrusions
item.description: Check Point Research demonstrated that peer influence can push an AI agent to violate established rules, with one agent's violation rate rising from 44 percent to 98 percent after repeated teammate behavior changes. The same report cites CERT-In reporting unauthorized access to organizational systems involving autonomous AI agents that exploited exposed credentials, insecure application interfaces, and misconfigured cloud services. Defenders should treat agent fleets as a monitored attack surface and rotate credentials reachable by agents.

item.title: Sekoia Flowise Honeypot Shows Attacker Turning Stolen AI Agent Into Offensive Assistant
item.description: Sekoia TDR deployed a Flowise honeypot and observed a threat actor steal its credentials, then attempt to repurpose the hosted AI agent as an interactive offensive assistant. The actor submitted real reconnaissance data on Nightingale and Redis infrastructure to generate custom exploitation playbooks targeting regional deployments. Defenders running AI orchestration platforms should treat stored LLM credentials and agent tool bindings as high value targets and restrict agent access to enterprise data and tools.

item.title: GhostAction Stage 2 Plants Font Disguised Credential Stealer in 94 GitHub Repositories
item.description: GhostAction operators escalated from malicious GitHub Actions workflows to a second stage that steals developer credentials without needing a workflow runner at all. Attackers planted a fake font file containing an infostealer that harvests AWS keys, PyPI and npm tokens, Kubernetes credentials, SSH private keys, and AI provider credentials for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini. Security teams should review repositories for the named file path, rotate exposed developer and cloud secrets, and audit GitHub OAuth app authorizations.
